column1: # THE TYPICAL YEAR (PLAN item 24): how a record's volatility is spread across its years.  The
# pooled vol anchor (`equity vol %`) cannot tell an ordinary year from an episode, so a search
# can close it by making every year more volatile; this file is the ruler that separates the two,
# and `typical-year vol %` in both twins is anchored on its medianYearVol rows.
# Per calendar year with at least 200 sessions: annualised RMS vol of daily LOG returns,
# sqrt(mean(r^2) * 252) * 100 -- the convention `equity vol %` uses, read one year at a time.
#   medianYearVol      the median of those yearly vols (the anchor; n = years)
#   pooledVol          the whole window's vol on the same convention (n = sessions)
#   p10YearVol, p90YearVol   the year distribution's tails
#   topDecileVarShare  the share of the window's summed r^2 in its most volatile tenth of years
# The model reads the same statistic over whole 252-session blocks of each path, median over
# blocks, then the median across paths.
# WHAT IT SETTLES.  QQQ over its whole history reads 0.68 of pooled where every other window
# and series reads 0.75-0.83: the Nasdaq anchor's 26.9 is a 27-year window whose volatility is
# ONE episode -- 2000, 2001 and 2002 at 58, 55 and 42% -- and QQQ from 2007 spreads its vol like
# SPY.  The model's Nasdaq recipe reads 0.81 on 27-year paths with a median year of 19.0, i.e.
# ON the record's ordinary year; the pooled gap is the bust.  CRSP from 1926 reads 0.75 for the
